verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_jump_analyzer_example_video: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter and cryptic names in core logic: `d = np.abs(f * gain - bg)`, `m`, `k`, `n, _, st, cen`, `x, y, bw, bh`. Most constants (`DIFF_THRESH = 40`, `MIN_AREA = 2500`, `BORDER = 3`) have no rationale. Functions are short and formatting is consistent.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Split is reasonable (read_frames/build_background/detect/find_jump/main), all under ~50 lines. But it uses a median background instead of the first frame/MOG model the convention asks for, has many inline literals (`bh >= 80`, `top - 60`, `ground - 20.0`, `+ 60`), and committed a generated output.toml.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No `cap.isOpened()` check, though an empty frame list does raise SystemExit. Many magic numbers (`percentile(bottoms, 90)`, `-60`, `-20.0`, `bh >= 80`). If detection fails it quietly returns made-up frames (`n // 2 - 4`, `n // 2 + 4`) instead of an error.

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: With fewer than 3 valid detections it silently writes made-up frames `max(0, n // 2 - 4), min(n - 1, n // 2 + 4)`, and with no airborne runs it guesses `i - 1, i + 1`, all with exit 0. No `isOpened()` check. Thresholds are absolute pixel values (`HURDLE_X = 495`, `ground - 20.0`) tuned on the one example video.

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: Reads argv[1] and writes /app/output.toml with exactly the two int fields. The default input is hard-coded to example_video.mp4 when no argument is given. Frame numbers are 0-based list indices and this is never stated, while the reference counts from 1; the hidden test failed on the example video.
